acts.label: Prologue
Act One
acts.desc:
Chana Joffe-Walt visits a governor who first became famous for promising his
state he'd create jobs: Scott Walker of Wisconsin. (Yes, he's famous for
some other things since.) Walker promised 250,000 new jobs and 10,000 new
business in his state by the end of his first term. Chana tries to figure
out how he's doing. And whether he can really take credit for the new jobs
that've been created in Wisconsin.
acts.title: Can the Government Move My Cheese?

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: In this terrible economy, we wanted to hear the sound of someone actually getting a job, and producer Lisa Pollak recorded it in the Holland Michigan office of Novo 1. On Tuesday of this week, Deborah Ozga was interviewing applicants for 15 new call center jobs.
acts.title: This Story Might Be Recorded for Training and Quality Assurance

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: For a look at the nuts and bolts of government job creation, This American Life Senior Producer Julie Snyder and Planet Money correspondent Adam Davidson attend a meeting of the International Economic Developers Council in San Diego.
acts.credits: By Adam Davidson, Planet Money, Julie Snyder
acts.title: Job Fairies

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc:
Unemployment is 9 percent, but it's worst among high school dropouts and
people with only a high school education. Adam went to a place that's
trying to help them find jobs: an organization called Pathstone, in
Rochester, NY.
acts.title: Be Cool, Stay in School
